verdict.rationale: Checkout.com's fraud-prevention docs include a section titled "Create risk rules and lists" plus fraud reports and fraud-detection testing, so a first-party custom risk-rules capability exists. The evidence is only a section heading, though; the AI-driven claim in docs-36 concerns acceptance-rate optimization, not fraud scoring. missing for 10: evidence of machine-learning fraud scores on transactions, documented block/review/allow rule actions, detail on rule-authoring depth, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a finance-ops user, I can screen transactions with machine-learning fraud scores and write custom block, review, and allow rules
